items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: the all night sessions you used to have in the New York with Tal Roney Farlow and Jimmy Rannie and Sal Salvador, talking and playing all night long

ctx.x: Yeah, they were all right, but, you know, he's like a chameleon, he just changes colors on those politics, you know.

You mentioned very briefly the all night sessions you used to have in the New York with Tal Roney Farlow and Jimmy Rannie and Sal Salvador, talking and playing all night long. Did you find those kind of sessions just with eachother more stimulating and productive than had you been playing for audiences?

Oh, naturally, because we could do it over, you know. And we exchanged ideas, and it was just the-- you know, it wasn't a frantic thing where we just played. We played until we, you know, got tired and we'd stop, we'd talk, have coffee, or something, just play. It was just good fellowship, you know, and that was quite enjoyable. Yeah, I enjoyed it.
